'''Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine''' (Takakuramusubimiko-jinja) is a shrine located in Aichi Prefecture Nagoya Atsuta Ward Takakura-cho. It is a Shikinaisha (Myōjin Taisha) and a Keigai-Sessha of Atsuta Shrine.

Like Atsuta Shrine, it enshrines the ancestral deity of Owari. Serving as the guardian and tutelary deity of the Takakura area, it is deeply revered locally and affectionately called "Takakura-sama."

== Worshipped deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|Saijin}}
The enshrined deity is the following one figure<ref name="HistoryDocument">Shrine History Document.</ref>:
* '''Takakura-shita-no-mikoto''' (Takakura-shita-no-mikoto)

== History ==
=== Founding ===
The founding is unknown. According to tradition, it may date to the reign of Emperor Tenmu (673–686)<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>, or it is said to have been established around the same time as the main shrine of Atsuta Shrine{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

Regarding the Keigai-Sessha of Atsuta Shrine—including Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine—there is a theory correlating its origins with the distribution of various Owari powers during the Kofun period<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488"/>. In this context, it is speculated that the dominant forces on the Atsuta plateau (such as Danpusan Kofun, Hakuchou Kofun, and Atsuta Shrine) absorbed other powers, resulting in the incorporation of various shrines into Atsuta Shrine's divine genealogy<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488">Shinshu Nagoya City History, Volume 1, Nagoya City, 1997, pp. 486–488.</ref>.

=== General History ===
According to the national histories (National Histories), the Zoku Nihon Kōki in the 2nd year of the Jōwa (836) contains a passage listing three deities of Atsuta Shrine—the Hiwari-mikogami, Mago-waka-mikogami, and the deity of Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Atsuta Ōkami Mikogami) – among the renowned deities{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

In the Enchō 5th year (927) version of the ''Engishiki'' (Jinmyōchō), in Owari Province's Aichi District, it is recorded as "Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine Myoujindai" and is listed alongside the Myōjin Taisha{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}. Moreover, in the Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō, it is recorded either as "Takakura Myōjin" or "Takakura Myōjin"{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

During the construction in the Genki era 2nd year (1571), there was a donation from Oda Nobunaga; in the Edo period, in the Genwa 4th year (1618), repairs were carried out by Hachisuka Iemasa, and in the Jōkyō era 3rd year (1686), when Atsuta Shrine was reconstructed by the Tokugawa shogunate, similar repairs were made to this shrine{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

The shrine building, originally in the Owari-zukuri style with a vermilion finish, was almost entirely destroyed by wartime damage in the Shōwa era 20th year (1945) and was rebuilt in a form approximating its pre-war appearance in the Shōwa era 38th year (1963){{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

=== Divine Rank ===
* Record of the conferral of divine Rank during the National Histories period:
** On December 12, in the 2nd year of the Jōwa (836), it was listed among the renowned deities (as recorded in the Zoku Nihon Kōki) – noted as "Takakurayui Mikoshi."
* After the era of the National Histories:
** Either Senior Second Rank<ref>[{{NDLDC|991014/413}} ''Shinja Kakoroku, Volume 1'' (Imperial Studies Institute, 1902, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 413 lines]</ref>, or Upper Senior Second Rank<ref>{{PDFlink|[https://websv.aichi-pref-library.jp/wahon/pdf/1103283156-001.pdf ''Domestic Shinmyōchō'']]} (Bunsei 13 [1830] transcribed combined edition, Aichi Prefectural Library "Precious Wa Books Digital Library") 6 lines.</ref>, or Junior Second Rank{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}} (in the Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō) – the inscription being "Takakura Myōjin" or "Takakura Myōjin"{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}. Note that the Ranking varies among manuscripts.

== Subordinate Shrines ==
Within the precincts, the following four subsidiary shrines are enshrined<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>. In the early modern period, it is said that there were also the Mitarai Shrine and the Kaijin Shrine.
* Hokotori Shrine – Enshrined deity: Hokotori-no-Kami
* Shingu Shrine – Enshrined deity: Susanoo
* Mii Shrine – Enshrined deity: Kimata-no-Kami
* Inari shrine – Enshrined deity: Ukanomitama
*: It is said that the mother of Toyotomi Hideyoshi (later known as Ōmandokoro) once took the young Hideyoshi with her to pray for his rise in life, which is why this shrine is also known by the alternate name "Taikō Shusse Inari."

== Festivals ==
* Inari Shrine Festival (on Hatsu-uma day)
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Spring Grand Festival (old Hatsu-uma day)
* Child Custody Festival (April 3)
*: A custom in which young children are entrusted to the enshrined deity until the age of 15, praying for healthy growth and protection from pests, with a subsequent thanksgiving visit once safely grown.
* Annual Festival (June 1)
* Mii Festival (on Doyō-iri day)
*: It is believed that if a child peers into the well of Mii Shrine on this day, it brings benefits of pest protection<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>.
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Autumn Grand Festival (November 8)
